indicators.description_short: Absolute number of votes a candidate received in a single AC contest.
Candidate votes as a percentage of total votes polled in the AC (including NOTA).

meta.justification: Candidate-grain measure: a single candidate's votes as a percentage of total votes polled in their AC (denominator = AC turnout including NOTA). Distinct from party-grain vote-share, which sums across all the party's candidates in the state.

indicators.description_short: Ordinal rank by votes polled (1 = winner).
Number of voters on the electoral roll for this AC as of election day.
Sum of all candidate votes plus NOTA in this AC contest.
Votes polled as a percentage of total enrolled electors.

indicators.label_long: Votes cast for NOTA in AC
indicators.description_short: Absolute number of NOTA (None of the Above) votes. Null pre-2013.
excluded_notes: NOTA was introduced by the Election Commission in 2013; pre-2013 values are null, not zero.

indicators.description_short: NOTA votes as a percentage of votes polled. Null pre-2013.
entity_id of the candidate who received the most votes. Stored in value_text.
party_id of the winning candidate's party (parties.IN.IND for independents).

meta.justification: AC-grain measure: party_id of the winning candidate in one Assembly Constituency contest (seat-level outcome). Distinct concept from state-grain twin which reports the state-aggregate majority-party id; denominators differ (single-seat plurality vs statewide seat-count majority).

indicators.description_short: Winner's votes minus runner-up's votes.

indicators.description_short: Vote-margin between winner and runner-up as a percentage of total votes polled.
1 / sum(vote_share_squared). Higher = more fragmented contest.

indicators.label_long: Vote share for candidates collapsed into the 'others' tail

Number of voters on the electoral roll for this Parliament PC as of election day.
Sum of all candidate votes plus NOTA in this Parliament PC contest.
Votes polled as a percentage of total enrolled electors in this Parliament PC.

indicators.description_short: Absolute number of NOTA (None of the Above) votes in this Parliament PC. Null pre-2013.
excluded_notes: NOTA was introduced by the Election Commission in 2013; pre-2013 values are null, not zero.

indicators.description_short: NOTA votes as a percentage of votes polled in this Parliament PC. Null pre-2013.
entity_id of the candidate who received the most votes in this Parliament PC. Stored in value_text.
party_id of the winning candidate's party in this Parliament PC (parties.IN.IND for independents).

meta.justification: PC-grain measure: party_id of the winning candidate in one Parliament parliamentary constituency contest (seat-level outcome). Genuinely new grain per ADR-0044 -- MP/PC is a different office on a different boundary than MLA/AC; mirrors the deliberate winning-party-ac / winning-party-state per-grain split. NOT a same-grain multi-publisher proliferation.

indicators.description_short: Winner's votes minus runner-up's votes in this Parliament PC.

indicators.label_long: Winning margin as % of votes polled (PC)
indicators.description_short: Vote-margin between winner and runner-up as a percentage of total votes polled in this Parliament PC.

indicators.label_long: Votes for candidates collapsed into the 'others' tail (PC)
indicators.description_short: Sum of votes for candidates below the top-N cutoff in this Parliament PC. Absent when no tail exists.

indicators.label_long: Vote share for candidates collapsed into the 'others' tail (PC)
indicators.description_short: Aggregate % vote-share for the collapsed tail in this Parliament PC. Absent when no tail exists.

indicators.label_long: Total candidates contesting the PC seat
indicators.description_short: Full field size in this Parliament PC: kept candidates plus those collapsed into the 'others' tail by the top-N cutoff.
1 / sum(vote_share_squared) in this Parliament PC. Higher = more fragmented contest.

indicators.label_long: ACs contested by party in state
indicators.description_short: Number of distinct ACs in the state where this party fielded a candidate.

indicators.label_long: PCs contested by party in state
indicators.description_short: Number of distinct parliamentary constituencies in the state where this party fielded a candidate.

indicators.label_long: ACs won by party in state

Seats won as a percentage of seats contested by the party.

indicators.label_long: Total votes polled by party in state

Party votes as a percentage of total votes polled in the state.

meta.justification: Party-grain measure: a party's votes summed across all its candidates as a percentage of total votes polled in the state (denominator = state turnout). Distinct from candidate-grain vote-share, which uses the AC turnout as denominator.

indicators.label_long: ACs where party candidate forfeited deposit
indicators.description_short: Number of ACs where the party's candidate received less than 1/6 of valid votes (Section 158, Representation of the People Act).
Sum of enrolled electors across all ACs in the state.
Sum of votes polled across all ACs in the state.
State-level votes polled as % of state-level enrolled electors.
Sum of NOTA votes across state as % of votes polled. Null pre-2013.
excluded_notes: NOTA introduced 2013; pre-2013 values are null, not zero.

indicators.description_short: 1 / sum(seat_share_squared) across parties. Higher = more fragmented legislature.
party_id with the most seats. Null in a hung-house outcome.

meta.justification: State-grain measure: party_id holding the most seats statewide (null on hung house). Distinct concept from AC-grain twin which reports per-seat winners; denominators differ (statewide seat-count majority vs single-seat plurality).

indicators.description_short: Seats held by the state's winning party.
floor(total_acs / 2) + 1. Constant per state per delimitation cycle.
Total nameplate generating capacity in megawatts, summed across all fuels, for India. Snapshot end-of-month from the CEA Monthly Executive Summary.
indicators.description_long: Nameplate capacity is the maximum sustained output a plant can deliver under ideal conditions â€” NOT the energy it actually produced. A state with high capacity isn't necessarily a high-generation state if those plants run at low plant-load factor (PLF). Compute-on-read parent: the value is the sum of the five atomic-fuel children (coal + gas + hydro + nuclear + renewable). No `_total_mw` row exists on disk (ADR-0030 D33.8 refusal).
indicators.methodology_vintage: CEA Monthly Executive Summary â€” Installed Capacity (IC) sheet; snapshot reported month-end. Sub-fuel taxonomy stable through current vintage; coal+lignite combined per CEA convention.

indicators.label_long: State installed electricity capacity, geographical-location basis (MW)
indicators.description_short: Total installed capacity physically located in the state, summed across all fuels. 'Geographical' means every plant counts toward the state where it sits, regardless of who owns it or where the power is dispatched.
indicators.description_long: Read this as 'where the steel-and-concrete sits' â€” NOT 'where the electricity flows to'. For the share-allocated counterpart (rights to output via central-sector PPAs), see installed-capacity-allocated-mw. The all-India total equals the allocated total (as it must) but the per-state breakdown diverges sharply for states that import or export power through central PPAs. Compute-on-read parent: sums the five atomic-fuel children.
indicators.methodology_vintage: NITI Aayog ICED capacity-metatable rollup of CEA-published station-level capacity; harmonised across fiscal years 2015-16 onwards.

indicators.label_long: State installed electricity capacity, allocated-shares basis (MW)
indicators.description_short: Same as the geographical-location capacity, but each state credited its share of joint-sector and central-sector plants per regional allocation formulas. Use this when comparing 'rights to electricity' rather than 'physical assets sited here'.
indicators.description_long: The all-India total equals the geographical total (as it must) but the per-state breakdown can diverge sharply: a state with little local capacity but large central-PPA shares has higher allocated capacity than geographical. Compute-on-read parent: sums the five atomic-fuel children.
indicators.methodology_vintage: NITI Aayog ICED state-wise deep-dive API for FY15-FY25 (fiscal years 2015-16 onwards); RBI Handbook of Statistics on Indian States, Table 140 (silver tier; republishes CEA originals) for the pre-FY15 splice (fiscal years 2004-05 to 2013-14). Per plan-doc 20260522 Â§3 Q-c Option 1 SPLICE: methodology break at FY15 (basis change + RBI portion carries no per-fuel breakdown).

indicators.label_long: Capacity allocated to state â€” Coal
indicators.description_short: Coal-fired thermal capacity. India's largest fuel category nationally (~42%).

meta.justification: State-grain BENEFICIARY share of plant capacity (ISGS/PSU contractual allocation). A Mundra plant sited in Gujarat is allocated to multiple states by quota. Distinct measure from -geographical- siting and from -snapshot- CEA-monthly cadence; each gets its own concept_id under guardrail #13.

indicators.label_long: Capacity allocated to state â€” Gas
indicators.description_short: Natural-gas and liquid-fuel thermal capacity. Stranded-fuel risk; small share.

meta.justification: State-grain BENEFICIARY share of plant capacity (ISGS/PSU contractual allocation). A Hazira plant sited in Gujarat is allocated across multiple states. Distinct from -geographical- twin; each now FKs to its own concept (gas-mw-{geographical,allocated,snapshot}).

indicators.label_long: Capacity allocated to state â€” Hydro
indicators.description_short: Conventional (>25 MW) plus small-hydro capacity. Site-bound; multi-decade lifetime.

meta.justification: State-grain BENEFICIARY share of plant capacity (ISGS/PSU contractual allocation). A large hydro station sited in one hill state is allocated across multiple consumer states. Distinct from -geographical- twin; each now FKs to its own concept (hydro-mw-{geographical,allocated,snapshot}).

indicators.label_long: Capacity allocated to state â€” Nuclear
indicators.description_short: Nuclear capacity. Central-sector only; allocated to states via PPAs.

meta.justification: State-grain BENEFICIARY share of nuclear capacity (NPCIL central-sector PPA allocation). A reactor sited in Tamil Nadu may be allocated to many consumer states by quota. Distinct measure from geographical siting and from CEA monthly snapshot.

indicators.label_long: Capacity allocated to state â€” Renewable (wind, solar, biomass)
indicators.description_short: Wind, solar, biomass and waste-to-energy. Rapid growth; ~30% national capacity by FY26.

meta.justification: State-grain BENEFICIARY share of renewable capacity (ISGS/PSU contractual allocation). A wind farm sited in Tamil Nadu may be allocated across multiple consumer states by quota. Distinct measure from geographical siting and from CEA monthly snapshot.

indicators.label_long: State installed electricity capacity â€” CEA monthly snapshot (MW)
indicators.description_short: Total installed capacity allocated to each state at the end of the most recent month, from the CEA Monthly Executive Summary IC sheet. Snapshot view; complements the multi-FY ICED geographical and allocated series.
indicators.description_long: End-of-month, point-in-time snapshot from the CEA Monthly Executive Summary 'IC' sheet. Allocation basis (where the power is dispatched, including central-sector PPA shares) â€” different from the geographical-location series which counts plants by where they physically sit. Compute-on-read parent: sums the five atomic-fuel children. Single vintage per release; restate on each fresh CEA monthly drop rather than appending â€” citizen comparability is snapshot-only across states, NOT a time series.
indicators.methodology_vintage: CEA Monthly Executive Summary â€” IC sheet snapshot 2026-03

indicators.description_short: Per-state actual electricity generated, summed across all fuels. The delivered counterpart to installed capacity â€” capacity is potential, generation is what plants actually produced.
indicators.description_long: Most-recent fiscal year is partial-year-actuals + forecast and may revise; treat the most-recent two FYs as preliminary. Compute-on-read parent: sums the five atomic-fuel children. ICED's 'Others' bucket (interstate/central plants pre-allocation) is dropped because it cannot be mapped to a state choropleth honestly. 1 MU (million unit) = 1 GWh.
indicators.methodology_vintage: NITI Aayog ICED /v1/gen-metatable-data (CEA-sourced upstream).

indicators.description_short: Coal-fired generation. ~70% of all-India electricity by GWh (PLF gap between capacity share and generation share).
Gas-fired generation. Capacity-rich, generation-poor due to fuel-supply constraints.
Hydroelectric generation. Seasonal (monsoon-dependent) and falling as a share over time.
Nuclear generation. Small share but rising as new units commission.

indicators.label_long: State generation (GWh) â€” Renewable (wind, solar, biomass)
indicators.description_short: Wind, solar and biomass generation. ~10% all-India share by FY26; growing fast.

Total electricity actually billed to end-consumers (domestic + commercial + industrial + agricultural + public-lighting) in the state, in million units (MU). The gap between Generation and Sales is the absolute AT&C loss.
indicators.methodology_vintage: NITI Aayog ICED state-wise deep-dive; underlying figures from PFC State Distribution Utilities report. Includes intra-state imports â€” consumption can exceed in-state generation.

indicators.label_long: Aggregate Technical & Commercial losses (%, by state)
indicators.description_short: Combined technical (transmission + distribution heat / ageing losses) and commercial (theft + uncollected billing) losses as % of energy input to the distribution system. Headline discom-health metric: lower is better.
indicators.description_long: Calculated by Power Finance Corporation from PFC State Distribution Utilities reports. UDAY (2015) targeted all-India AT&C below 15% by 2018-19; the actual all-India figure has hovered around 15% since then. State-level dispersion is wide â€” Gujarat / Andhra at ~6-10%, Bihar / J&K at ~25-40%.
indicators.methodology_vintage: NITI Aayog ICED state-wise deep-dive API row 'AT&C Losses'. Calculation method: PFC. Vintage updated annually with PFC report release (typically Q3 FY+1).

indicators.description_short: Highest single-instant electricity demand observed in the state during the fiscal year (MW). 'Peak' is system-wide simultaneous demand recorded by the State Load Despatch Centre â€” typically a summer afternoon (north / west) or winter evening (Punjab, Delhi).
indicators.description_long: Read alongside Peak Met (peak-electricity-supplied-mw) â€” the gap is the unmet peak demand, more operationally critical than the energy-deficit % because shortages force load-shedding. RBI Handbook relabelled 'Surplus / Deficit' to 'Demand Not Met' from FY 2019-20 onwards; underlying definition is unchanged.
indicators.methodology_vintage: RBI Handbook of Statistics on Indian States 2024-25 edition, Table 142. Originating data: Central Electricity Authority, Ministry of Power.

indicators.description_short: Maximum instantaneous power actually supplied in the state during the fiscal year (MW). The pair (peak_demand, peak_supplied) tells the load-shedding story: supplied < demand in any year means the grid dropped load to keep frequency stable.
indicators.description_long: India's all-India peak deficit fell from ~12% in FY05 to under 1% from FY18 onwards, but state-level shortfalls persist â€” Bihar, UP, Punjab, J&K, and Andhra Pradesh routinely under-met their own peak in the FY13-FY25 window.
indicators.methodology_vintage: RBI Handbook of Statistics on Indian States 2024-25 edition, Table 142 (Peak Met column). Originating data: Central Electricity Authority.

indicators.description_short: Electricity consumption per person per year, in kilowatt-hours. Proxy for BOTH energy access (electrified homes) AND industrial intensity (heavy-industry load) â€” read alongside per-capita income to disambiguate.
indicators.description_long: A high value can mean many electrified domestic consumers (Kerala) OR a heavy-industry economy (Chhattisgarh, Odisha) OR both (Gujarat). A low value can mean a rural agrarian economy (Bihar, Assam) OR poor access (UP). The denominator (population) is Census 2011 + projection, so values for the 2020s are subject to mid-decade re-basing once Census 2027 data lands.
indicators.methodology_vintage: ICED composition: state electricity sales (CEA) divided by state population (Census 2011 + linear projection).

indicators.description_short: Compute-on-read parent: the three citizen-readable sub-indicators of distribution-side efficiency â€” billing efficiency, collection efficiency, and T&D loss. The first two decompose the COMMERCIAL half of AT&C losses; the third is the TECHNICAL half.
indicators.description_long: Billing Ã— Collection Ã· 100 = (1 âˆ’ commercial-loss%); add the T&D loss% and you arrive at the AT&C loss% reported by atc-losses-pct. Per Hans D29 the parent row carries no source_id and no dimension_values; the three children inherit their source_id from ICED operational-performance and encode their facet via the efficiency_dimension axis.
indicators.methodology_vintage: NITI Aayog ICED `/energy/electricity/distribution/operationalPerformanceStates`. Three categories: `billing-efficiency`, `collection-efficiency`, `td-loss`.

indicators.description_short: Share of energy actually billed to a consumer, out of total energy input to the distribution system. 100% = every kWh that enters the grid was billed.
indicators.description_long: The complement of billing-side losses (theft, unmetered consumption, under-billing). Together with collection efficiency, billing efficiency decomposes the commercial half of AT&C losses: AT&C loss â‰ˆ 1 âˆ’ (billing Ã— collection / 100).

indicators.description_short: Share of billed revenue actually collected from consumers, by state. 100% = every rupee billed was paid.
indicators.description_long: Captures the second commercial dimension: how much of the energy that WAS billed got paid for. Together with billing efficiency, collection efficiency decomposes the commercial half of AT&C losses: AT&C loss â‰ˆ 1 âˆ’ (billing Ã— collection / 100). Low collection often reflects high accounts-receivable days on government / agricultural / municipal consumer categories.

indicators.description_short: Transmission and Distribution loss as % of energy input â€” the TECHNICAL half of AT&C losses (heat / ageing / unmetered consumption on the wires).
indicators.description_long: T&D loss + commercial-loss = AT&C loss. Where AT&C is a comprehensive ledger of revenue leakage, T&D isolates the part attributable to physical infrastructure (line losses, transformer inefficiency). Older meters and longer rural feeders correlate with higher T&D loss; sub-station upgrades and HVDS rollout drive it down.

indicators.label_long: ACS-ARR gap on electricity sales (â‚¹/kWh, by state)
indicators.description_short: Average Cost of Supply minus Average Revenue Realised, per unit of electricity sold. Positive = the utility loses money on every unit it sells (closed by tariff hike, loss reduction, or state subsidy). Zero is the UDAY/RDSS policy goal.
indicators.description_long: The structural per-unit loss of a discom: positive means it loses money on every kWh sold; negative means surplus. Calculated by PFC from utility tariff orders + audited accounts. Note the opposite sign convention from fiscal-deficit indicators â€” here a NEGATIVE number is the surplus side.
indicators.methodology_vintage: NITI Aayog ICED state-wise deep-dive row 'ACS-ARR (Electricity Sales) Gap'. Calculated by PFC from utility tariff orders + audited accounts.

indicators.label_long: Renewable Purchase Obligation compliance (%, by state)
indicators.description_short: Compute-on-read parent: the three citizen-readable segments of state RPO compliance â€” solar, non-solar, and combined-target. Each measures share of the regulatory RPO target met, expressed as compliance Ã· target Ã— 100.
indicators.description_long: Each state regulator sets a year-by-year RPO target as a % of total energy procurement; this parent groups the three segment-specific compliance ratios. The 'total' segment is NOT the sum of solar + non-solar â€” it is the combined-target compliance ratio (its own regulatory denominator). Values above 100% indicate over-compliance. Targets themselves vary by state and rise over time, so a 95% compliance in FY21 may represent more renewables than 105% in FY19.
indicators.methodology_vintage: NITI Aayog ICED `/energy/electricity/distribution/rpo` (MNRE / state-regulator data). Three facets: `solar` (solarCompliance), `non-solar` (nonSolarCompliance), `total` (totalCompliance).

indicators.label_long: RPO compliance â€” solar (%, by state)
indicators.description_short: Share of the state's solar-specific RPO target actually met. 100% = solar-RPO target exactly met; values above 100% indicate over-compliance on solar procurement.

indicators.label_long: RPO compliance â€” non-solar (%, by state)
indicators.description_short: Share of the state's non-solar (wind + biomass + small-hydro) RPO target actually met. The 'other-renewables' segment of the obligation, regulated separately from the solar segment.

indicators.label_long: RPO compliance â€” total (%, by state)
indicators.description_short: Combined-target RPO compliance â€” share of the state's overall (solar + non-solar combined) RPO target met. NOT the sum of solar + non-solar â€” the combined target is its own regulatory ratio.

Annual energy requirement assessed by the state (MU = million units = GWh), fiscal year â€” the demand-side counterpart to availability. Requirement minus availability gives the 'energy not supplied' deficit.
indicators.description_long: The percentage gap (deficit / requirement) is the headline 'power deficit %' India tracked closely through the 2000s. The all-India deficit shrank from ~10% in FY05 to under 0.5% from FY18 onwards as supply caught up; persistent state-level deficits today flag distribution / scheduling issues, not generation shortage. Direction is neutral because higher requirement reflects both industrial activity (good) and inefficient consumption (not good) â€” interpret in conjunction with per-capita GSDP and T&D loss series.
indicators.methodology_vintage: RBI Handbook of Statistics on Indian States 2024-25 edition, Table 141. Originating data: Central Electricity Authority, Ministry of Power.

indicators.description_short: Annual energy actually supplied to the state (MU = million units = GWh), fiscal year. The supply-side companion to Requirement (T141). Requirement âˆ’ Availability = the energy-not-supplied deficit.
indicators.description_long: RBI Handbook Table 139 publishes the long-arc state-wise availability series sourced from CEA. Read alongside Requirement (T141): the percentage gap is the operational power-deficit metric. The all-India figure has converged on near-zero deficit since FY18, but state-level deficits persist for grid-island / load-shedding states.
indicators.methodology_vintage: RBI Handbook of Statistics on Indian States 2024-25 edition, Table 139. Originating data: Central Electricity Authority, Ministry of Power.

indicators.description_short: Annual per-capita electricity availability (kWh / person / year), by state and Union Territory, fiscal year. The most citizen-relevant single number for 'how much power do people in this state actually get to use' â€” captures both supply expansion and transmission losses.
indicators.description_long: Computed by CEA as state energy availability (MU) Ã· state mid-year population. The all-India figure roughly tripled from ~600 kWh in FY05 to ~1300 kWh in FY24, but the inter-state spread is wide (Goa / Punjab / Gujarat above 2,000; Bihar / Manipur / Nagaland still below 400). Per-capita is on geographical-area population (resident), not consumption-weighted â€” large industrial-export states (e.g. Chhattisgarh, Sikkim) post inflated numbers because the power they generate is consumed elsewhere.
indicators.methodology_vintage: RBI Handbook of Statistics on Indian States 2024-25 edition, Table 138. Originating data: Central Electricity Authority, Ministry of Power.

indicators.label_long: State coal consumption (Mt, by fiscal year)
indicators.description_short: Per-state domestic coal consumption in million tonnes per fiscal year, summed across all coal grades (raw + washed + middlings + lignite). High values typically indicate hosting large thermal generation fleets (Maharashtra, UP, MP, Chhattisgarh) or heavy industry (steel, cement).
indicators.description_long: Where coal is burned, not where it is mined. Companion to installed-capacity-allocated-mw (coal facet) and electricity-generation-gwh (coal facet): a state with high coal consumption but low coal generation is using coal for industrial heat rather than power. The ``TOTAL COAL`` ICED rows are dropped to avoid double-counting; the lift sums the 4 grade-level rows (raw + washed + middlings + lignite) directly.
indicators.methodology_vintage: NITI Aayog ICED ``/energy/fuel-sources/coal/consumption-domestic-state`` (Coal Controller's Office / Ministry of Coal upstream). Aggregated by SUM of the 4 component grades (raw, washed, middlings, lignite); the precomputed ``TOTAL COAL`` rows are dropped to avoid double-counting.

indicators.description_short: Cumulative installed rooftop solar PV capacity in megawatts. Building-mounted (residential + commercial + industrial + public) only; utility-scale solar is separate and lives under installed-capacity-snapshot-mw (renewable facet).
indicators.description_long: Per the National Rooftop Solar Programme (MNRE), rooftop solar is owned by the building owner (household, factory, school), not by a power utility. A state's total solar fleet = rooftop + utility-scale. Gujarat dominates rooftop deployment by absolute MW (a decade of state-level scheme co-funding plus the SURYA Gujarat residential push). Rajasthan and Karnataka lead utility-scale solar but lag on rooftop because rooftop economics depend on retail tariff structure (which favours states with high commercial tariffs like Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu) more than insolation. Pair with installed-capacity-snapshot-mw (renewable facet) to see whether a state's renewable footprint is utility-investor-led or owner-led.
indicators.methodology_vintage: NITI Aayog ICED ``/energy/renewable/solar/rooftop/state``. Originating data: MNRE / state nodal agencies via the National Rooftop Solar Programme. ICED is the federal aggregator; not the issuing authority.

indicators.label_long: India thermal generating capacity retired, by fuel (MW per year)
indicators.description_short: National total of thermal generating capacity retired each fiscal year, broken down by fuel (coal vs gas). A key signal in the energy-transition story: rising coal retirements means the fleet is being replaced, not just expanded.
indicators.description_long: Annual MW of utility-scale thermal generating capacity retired across India, broken into 2 fuel buckets (coal + gas; ICED's 'oil-gas' label collapses into the canonical 'gas' bucket per indicator-naming.md). Pair with installed-capacity additions to read net change. National-only -- ICED does NOT publish state-level retired capacity. Captures only utility-scale thermal retirements; captive plants and renewables decommissioning are out of scope of the upstream feed. Compute-on-read parent: sums the 2 atomic-fuel children.
indicators.methodology_vintage: NITI Aayog ICED ``/v1/retired-capacity-plants``. Originating data: Central Electricity Authority station-level retirement records. ICED is the federal aggregator; not the issuing authority.

indicators.description_short: Coal-fired thermal capacity retired each fiscal year. The dominant retired-capacity category (~90% of cumulative thermal retirements since FY05).

meta.justification: Country-grain RETIREMENTS flow (capacity decommissioned per FY), not stock. Distinct concept from -installed- which is end-of-period live capacity per Hans identity rule (different measure).

indicators.description_short: Gas-fired thermal capacity retired each fiscal year. Includes oil-fired and diesel-fired thermal capacity (ICED's publisher label is 'oil-gas'; canonical bucket is 'gas' per Hans D33.8). Small fleet; sporadic retirements.

meta.justification: Country-grain RETIREMENTS flow (capacity decommissioned per FY), not stock. Includes oil-fired and diesel-fired (ICED publisher label "oil-gas"; canonical bucket per Hans D33.8). Distinct concept from -installed- per Hans identity rule (different measure).

indicators.label_long: State oil-product consumption, by product (kt per fiscal year)
indicators.description_short: Per-state annual consumption of refined petroleum products in kilotonnes, broken down by 7 products (diesel-HSD, petrol, LPG, kerosene, naphtha, petroleum-coke, others). Diesel dominates everywhere; LPG tracks PMUY rollout; petroleum-coke tracks industrial heat use.
indicators.description_long: Consumption-side oil statistic: where the product is sold and burned, not where it is refined. Faceted on the canonical ``oil_product`` axis (7 product children). Compute-on-read parent: the value is the sum of the 7 product children, per Hans D33.8 convention. No observation rows exist on disk for this parent id; the renderer sums the 7 children at read time. Originating data: PPAC / Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas (via NITI Aayog ICED).
indicators.methodology_vintage: NITI Aayog ICED ``/energy/fuel-sources/oil/consumptionStateProductTrend`` (PPAC / Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas upstream). Per-state per-product per-FY, FY11-FY25. The ``OTHERS`` state bucket and the national aggregate row (region == ``IN``) are dropped at ingest.

indicators.description_short: High-speed diesel: the dominant refined petroleum product. Tracks transport activity (heavy vehicles, buses, trucks) and agricultural pump-set use; the largest single fuel by volume in every state.
Motor spirit (gasoline): cars, two-wheelers, light vehicles. A proxy for urban-personal-mobility intensity; rises with vehicle ownership and middle-class growth.

Liquefied petroleum gas: household cooking-fuel after the PMUY (Ujjwala) scheme. Tracks household-coverage policy more than wealth -- rural states with successful PMUY rollout show high per-capita LPG consumption.
Superior kerosene oil: household lighting + cooking fuel from the legacy PDS era. Declines steeply post-PMUY as LPG replaces it; near-zero in many states by FY23.
Light hydrocarbon feedstock for petrochemicals + occasional power-plant fuel. Concentrated in petrochemical-cluster states (Gujarat, Maharashtra). Volatile year-on-year.
Refinery by-product used as cheap industrial fuel (cement, glass, steel). Heavily regulated for air-quality reasons in NCR and some industrial states. Tracks heavy-industry heat use.
Publisher catch-all for products outside the 6 named buckets (fuel oil, ATF, lubricants, bitumen, etc.). Preserved verbatim, never imputed into a named bucket.

indicators.label_long: India total primary energy supply (TPES), by source (mtoe per fiscal year)
indicators.description_short: Annual total primary energy supply for India, broken down by source (coal, oil, gas, hydro, nuclear, renewables). The TPES denominator behind every per-capita / per-GDP energy intensity calculation.
indicators.description_long: Total Primary Energy Supply (TPES) is the sum of indigenous production plus net imports of energy commodities, expressed in million tonnes of oil equivalent (mtoe). 6 atomic-fuel children (coal + oil + gas + hydro + nuclear + renewable) on the canonical fuel_type axis; publisher emits a per-fuel value plus a `total` row which is FILTERED at canonical lift (compute-on-read parent: total = SUM of children). National-only -- ICED does NOT publish state-level TPES. Originating data: MoSPI Energy Statistics India; republished via NITI Aayog ICED.
indicators.methodology_vintage: NITI Aayog ICED ``/analytics/state-wise-deep-dive`` (primary-energy-supply national series). Originating data: MoSPI Energy Statistics India (annual edition). ICED is the federal aggregator; not the issuing authority.

indicators.description_short: Coal share of total primary energy supply. The dominant TPES bucket since FY05 (~55% in recent years).
Crude-oil + petroleum-products share of TPES. The second-largest bucket; tracks transport-fleet activity and refinery throughput.

indicators.label_long: India primary energy supply -- Natural gas
indicators.description_short: Natural-gas share of TPES (domestic + LNG imports). The fastest-growing fossil bucket; tracks LNG-terminal commissioning and pipeline expansion.
Large hydro share of TPES (>=25 MW). Inter-annual swings track monsoon variability; structurally flat as no major new dams have been commissioned recently.
Nuclear share of TPES. Small fleet (~7 GW operational); structurally flat with episodic step changes when a new reactor commissions.
Aggregate renewable share of TPES (solar + wind + biomass + small-hydro + waste-to-energy). The fastest-growing bucket; publisher emits as a single aggregate, not broken into RE sub-fuels.

indicators.label_long: State plant load factor (PLF) by fuel source (%)
indicators.description_short: Share of nameplate capacity actually delivered as energy over a fiscal year. Per state, per fuel source. Coal PLFs near 60% indicate healthy merit-order despatch; near 40% indicates structural underuse.
Coal-fired plant load factor: how hard the state's coal fleet is being run. 60%+ = healthy despatch, 40% = structural underuse (stranded assets), regulator-set floor varies.

indicators.label_long: State plant load factor -- Gas (oil + diesel + furnace oil + natural gas) (%)
indicators.description_short: Gas-fired plant load factor (publisher bucket 'oil-gas' = natural gas + diesel + furnace oil). Persistently low in India (often <25%) due to gas allocation shortages -- not a despatch failure.

indicators.label_long: State plant load factor -- Large hydro (%)
indicators.description_short: Large-hydro plant load factor (capacity > 25 MW). Inherently seasonal; monsoon-dependent states show high inter-year variation that is RESOURCE-driven, not fleet-performance-driven.
Nuclear plant load factor. Only present in states hosting reactors (TN/Karnataka/Rajasthan/Gujarat/Maharashtra/UP); rest = no data. Targets 80%+ when fuel-supply and grid-offtake align.

indicators.label_long: State plant load factor -- Small hydro (<= 25 MW) (%)
indicators.description_short: Small-hydro plant load factor (capacity <= 25 MW). Run-of-river dominated; seasonal-flow-bounded. Distinct from large-hydro for despatch and resource-availability reasons.

Solar PLF (utility + rooftop combined). Resource-bounded: even perfect operation cannot exceed ~22-25% in India (function of sunlight hours). A 20% solar PLF is GOOD; do NOT compare to a 60% coal target.

Wind PLF. Resource-bounded by site quality (Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Karnataka coastal/desert zones are wind-rich). A 25% wind PLF in Tamil Nadu is excellent; same number in a low-wind state could be aspirational siting.

indicators.label_long: State plant load factor -- Biomass / bio-power (%)
indicators.description_short: Biomass / bio-power PLF (publisher label: 'bio-power'). Feedstock-supply-bounded; agricultural-residue-rich states (Punjab, Haryana, UP, Tamil Nadu) show higher PLFs only when supply chains are functional.

Share of total electricity purchased by a state's distribution utilities, broken down by generation source. The procurement mix (where DISCOMs buy from), not the generation mix (what plants produce). Values sum to ~100% per (state, FY).

Share of state's procured electricity that came from coal plants. India-wide ~70% historically; declining as RE rises. Coal-importing states (Karnataka, Maharashtra, Punjab) typically run above the average.

indicators.label_long: State power-purchase share -- Gas (oil + diesel + natural gas) (%)
indicators.description_short: Gas-fired procurement share (publisher 'oil-gas' bucket: natural gas + furnace oil). Often <5% due to gas-allocation shortages limiting plant availability.
Diesel-genset procurement share. Typically <1% across most states; an emergency-backup category, not a baseload source.
Large-hydro (>25 MW) procurement share. Higher in hill states (HP, UK, Sikkim) and seasonally variable across monsoon vs winter.
Nuclear procurement share. Allocated centrally from NPCIL plants; states near reactors (TN, KA, MH, RJ, GJ, UP) have higher shares.

indicators.label_long: State power-purchase share -- Small hydro (<= 25 MW) (%)
indicators.description_short: Small-hydro (<=25 MW) procurement share. Distinct from large hydro; counts under most state RPO obligations.
Solar procurement share (utility + rooftop). Rajasthan, Gujarat, Karnataka lead with double-digit shares; smaller eastern states still in single digits.
Wind procurement share. Resource-bounded; Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Rajasthan dominate as both producers AND consumers (sold within state and via inter-state PPAs).
Biomass / bio-power procurement share. Tied to agri-residue feedstock availability; meaningful in Punjab, Haryana, UP, Tamil Nadu when supply chains function.

indicators.label_long: State power-purchase share -- Other renewables (waste-to-energy + uncategorised RE) (%)
indicators.description_short: Other-renewables procurement share (publisher 'other-res' bucket): waste-to-energy and small uncategorised RE. Typically <1-2% across most states.

indicators.label_long: State power-purchase share -- Hybrid (bundled wind + solar + storage) (%)
indicators.description_short: Bundled-hybrid PPA procurement share (wind + solar + storage sold as one contract). A procurement-channel category, not a single fuel. Emerging post-2022 as MNRE hybrid policy ramped.

indicators.label_long: State power-purchase share -- Power-exchange trading + UI mechanisms (%)
indicators.description_short: Procurement via power exchanges (IEX / PXIL) + unscheduled interchange (UI). Source-agnostic at procurement time. Higher trading share = state buys spot to meet demand fluctuations, not necessarily a stress signal.

indicators.label_long: India final energy consumption by sector and source (mtoe)
indicators.description_short: Final energy consumption in India broken down by end-use sector x fuel (18 pairs). Final = what households / industry actually USE (post-conversion losses), distinct from TPES (primary supply).

Final energy consumed in the commercial sector via electricity, in mtoe per fiscal year.
Final energy consumed in the commercial sector via oil, in mtoe per fiscal year.

indicators.label_long: State installed grid-connected renewable capacity (MW, end-March snapshot)
indicators.description_short: Cumulative grid-connected renewable installed capacity in MW, end-March snapshot per year. Combined wind + solar + small-hydro + biomass + waste-to-energy (publisher emits no per-source split). Rajasthan, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Maharashtra dominate.
Count of animals issued a 12-digit Pashu Aadhaar tag in each district. Tagged count, NOT actual population.
indicators.description_long: Pashu Aadhaar is the UIDAI-style 12-digit unique identifier issued by the National Digital Livestock Mission (NDLM, Bharat Pashudhan) to individual animals. The count here is the number of TAGS issued in each district, NOT an estimate of the actual livestock population - coverage varies by state as the rollout is in progress. Compute-on-read parent: the value is the sum of the 10 atomic-species children (cattle + buffalo + yak + mithun + sheep + goat + pig + horse + donkey + mule). No observation rows exist on disk for this id (per Hans D33.8 convention); the frontend sums the children at read time. The catalogue carries comparability=directional_only and renderer_rules=[no_rank_table] - the renderer suppresses rank-table views and labels the choropleth illustrative, not a ranking.
indicators.methodology_vintage: NDLM Bharat Pashudhan; snapshot 2026-05 covers FY 2010-11..2025-26 (16 annual vintages from one operator snapshot). NDLM Bharat Pashudhan portal rolled out around 2018; tag counts are cumulative-since-rollout, so earlier FYs may show small or zero values where the registry was not yet operating in that district.

Same Hans honest-renderer caveat applies: tagged count is NOT an estimate of the actual cattle population of the district; coverage varies by state. indicators.description_short: Count of livestock owners completed Bharat Pashudhan registration in each district. Registered count, NOT all owning households.
indicators.description_long: Owner Registration is the Bharat Pashudhan workflow that records a livestock-owner profile (name + landholding bracket + gender) before any Pashu Aadhaar tag can be issued to that owner's animals. The count here is the number of REGISTERED owners in each district per the National Digital Livestock Mission (NDLM), NOT an estimate of the total livestock-owning households - coverage varies by state as the rollout is in progress. Compute-on-read parent: the value is the sum of the 6 atomic land-holding bracket children (landless_marginal + small + semi_medium + medium + large + not_specified). No observation rows exist on disk for this id (per Hans D33.8 convention); the frontend sums the children at read time. The publisher also disaggregates by gender (male/female); this slice collapses the gender axis via SUM at write time and lifts on landholding only (gender retained in the meadow for a follow-up PR). The catalogue carries comparability=directional_only and renderer_rules=[no_rank_table] - the renderer suppresses rank-table views and labels the choropleth illustrative, not a ranking.

NDLM Bharat Pashudhan portal rolled out around 2018; tag counts are cumulative-since-rollout, so earlier FYs may show small or zero values where the registry was not yet operating in that district.

meta.justification: District SoT with state-grain SUM rollup per ADR-0043; same publisher cell, same source_id, same period_label, distinguished only by entity_id grain (district vs state prefix). indicators.label_long: NAIP IV ai events (district SoT, auto-rolled to state per ADR-0043)
indicators.description_short: Count of artificial-insemination EVENTS performed in each district under NAIP IV. Repeat inseminations on the same animal are counted multiple times.
indicators.description_long: NAIP IV (National Artificial Insemination Programme, phase IV) is a select-district programme administered by the Department of Animal Husbandry & Dairying (DAHD). Each row counts artificial-insemination EVENTS performed in the district during FY 2024-25 - NOT unique animals inseminated. Repeat inseminations on the same dam are counted multiple times (an animal may need 2-3 cycles before conception). 8 states/UTs (Kerala, Punjab, Puducherry, Chandigarh, Delhi, Lakshadweep, A&N, D&NH+D&D) report zero coverage upstream and are GENUINELY ABSENT from this fact-table - that is correct, not a defect: NAIP IV is select-district, and a missing state means out-of-scope, not zero-result. Catalogue carries comparability=directional_only and renderer_rules=[no_rank_table] - the renderer suppresses rank-table views and labels the choropleth illustrative.

indicators.label_long: All-India under-construction generation capacity by expected commissioning year (GW)
indicators.description_short: Future thermal generation capacity in active construction across India, summed across pipeline statuses (likely to be commissioned + on hold), bucketed by the calendar year the plant is expected to come online. Distinct from already-installed capacity.
indicators.description_long: ICED plantPipelineInfo reports under-construction capacity by expected commissioning calendar-year, split into two status facets ('Under Construction and likely to be commissioned' vs 'Under Construction but on Hold'). This canonical row sums the two facets to one TOTAL pipeline GW per year; the status breakdown is preserved in the meadow JSON for a potential future facet-children PR. Publisher series spans 2011-2031 with a 2022 gap preserved verbatim. National grain only -- ICED does not publish per-state pipeline. Originating data: Central Electricity Authority station-level pipeline records; ICED is the federal aggregator (silver / not-authority per Hans D33 + plan-doc §3 Q-d).
indicators.methodology_vintage: ICED plantPipelineInfo endpoint snapshot 2026-05-27; monthly publisher cadence. Calendar-year expected-commissioning grain. AES-encrypted upstream envelope; IcedClient.get(..., decrypt=True). Status SUM-collapse over the 2 publisher facets at adapter time.

meta.justification: First ingest through the 4-layer doctrine + ADR-0046 pre-flight gate; verdict mint_new (no existing concept scored ≥0.70 against (under-construction-capacity, GW, absolute, country)). Distinct concept from `all-india-installed-capacity` (commissioned + grid-synchronised stock) because pipeline capacity is a FORWARD-LOOKING flow measure of plants not yet on the grid; same fuel, different physical state -- not a facet collapse candidate per ADR-0044 concept-identity doctrine.

indicators.description_short: NITI Aayog SDG India Index composite score (0-100): a state/UT's distance to the 2030 Sustainable Development Goal targets.
indicators.description_long: NITI Aayog's SDG India Index scores each state and UT from 0 to 100 on its distance to the 2030 SDG targets, aggregating the goal-wise scores NITI computes from a basket of official indicators. 100 means every tracked target is met; the national (India) figure is the population-weighted aggregate. The index is a governance / policy dashboard, not a direct outcome measure, and NITI revises the indicator basket and methodology each edition (2018, 2019-20, 2020-21, 2023-24), so a score is comparable across states within one edition but not cleanly across editions (hence comparability = comparable_across_states_snapshot_only).

meta.justification: First NITI SDG India Index ingest via the run_pipeline single-series pipeline; verdict mint_new (top concept-overlap score 0.388 < 0.70 against (SDG India Index score, score, index, state)). A composite policy-dashboard index distinct from every existing concept; not a grain or facet of another measure, so no facet-collapse per ADR-0044.
